title: Preprocessor directives, macros and conditional compilation
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its C rules.
Trace the example and identify data or control flow.
Recognize common failure and safety cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: The preprocessor handles directives such as #include, #define, #if, #ifdef and #endif before the compiler processes the resulting translation unit. Object-like and function-like macros perform token substitution and can affect code in ways that ordinary functions do not.
understand.whyItMatters: Preprocessor features support configuration and shared constants, but macros lack normal function type checking and may evaluate arguments more than once.
understand.analogy: Treat each resource and operation as having a clear contract, valid lifetime and failure path.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, compiler or library specifications.

explain.narrative:
The preprocessor handles directives such as #include, #define, #if, #ifdef and #endif before the compiler processes the resulting translation unit. Object-like and function-like macros perform token substitution and can affect code in ways that ordinary functions do not.

Check object bounds, lifetimes, arithmetic limits and all relevant return values. Compile with warnings enabled and test both normal and failure paths.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: Parentheses protect the macro argument and the full replacement expression from many precedence problems. Even so, passing an expression with side effects can evaluate it more than once.

practise.guidedTask: Expand SQUARE(value + 1) mentally and explain the parentheses.
practise.independentTask: Create a header guard and a configuration macro. Explain what code is included under each condition.
hints: Prefer functions or const objects when they provide safer semantics than macros.
Macro arguments may be substituted multiple times; avoid side effects in arguments.
Use unique macro names and parenthesize macro parameters and replacement expressions.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable way to protect correctness?
options: Validate preconditions, bounds and failure results.
Ignore the type and lifetime rules.
questions.answer: Validate preconditions, bounds and failure results.
questions.explanation: C requires explicit handling of object validity and operation failures.

questions.prompt: How should the example be checked?
options: Compile with warnings and test expected and failure cases.
Ignore diagnostics and test only once.
questions.answer: Compile with warnings and test expected and failure cases.
questions.explanation: Warnings and targeted tests provide evidence for correctness.
